set_aside.subject: grant_producer_project
set_aside.text: - grant_producer_project: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST decide the project from the validation result alone, reading its declared exists and is_active fields directly: a project the registry does not know is a scoped not-found rejection, and a project it knows but reports inactive is the archived rejection. It MUST NOT reach those values through a defensive attribute lookup with a default, which turns every validation into "not active" and refuses every grant while looking like a registry answer rather than a defect, and it MUST NOT ask the registry for a second, richer answer to decide the same thing twice. That call MUST happen while no transaction of this function is open, because a transaction must never stay open across a network call.
set_aside.question: Must the deleted no-argument constructor contract for ArchivedProjectRejected be restored, or must the requirement specify how the archived rejection is constructed?
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: issue_service_credential
set_aside.text: - issue_service_credential: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST issue a credential only when the addressed ServicePrincipal has ACTIVE status. A principal with any other status MUST raise AuthorizationRejected without generating a secret, inserting a credential, or appending an audit, and the open transaction MUST close.
set_aside.question: Must the deleted no-argument constructor contract for AuthorizationRejected be restored, or must the requirement specify how AuthorizationRejected is constructed?

set_aside.subject: ScopedNotFoundError requirements
set_aside.text: - revoke_producer_project: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST answer with the scoped not-found rejection whenever the grant cannot be revoked — it does not exist, or it exists but is already revoked — and MUST NOT tell those two apart. A grant that is already revoked is no longer a revocable target, so reporting it differently would let a caller probe which grant identifiers were ever issued while adding nothing an administrator can act on.
set_aside.question: Must the deleted no-argument constructor contract for ScopedNotFoundError be restored, or must the requirements specify how the scoped not-found rejection is constructed?
